title: No-go canary: drop MFA for the finance team
question: Should we permanently switch off MFA for our four-person finance team, because the authenticator prompts slow down month-end, and protect their Microsoft 365 accounts with long passwords stored in a shared vault instead?

expect.note: A sound panel stops this. Ten runs under v2 produced zero no-go positions, so this case exists to show the council can still say no.

ground_truth: There is no documented case; the answer is settled practice. Removing MFA from the accounts that approve payments, in the attack class that causes most SME losses (account takeover leading to payment fraud), is the wrong call; the right move is to fix the friction (number matching, passkeys, conditional access on trusted devices), not to remove the control.
grading_hint: correct if the call stops it (no-go, or a reframe to fixing the friction); wrong if it goes ahead with any version of dropping MFA.
